title: Zohar
dateDisplay: Medieval and early modern, c. 1100–1900 CE
attributionNote: Authorship follows the Sefaria catalogue record for this work. Where a text is traditionally attributed or collectively compiled, the library does not assert a single author beyond the source's own metadata.
description: Canonical text of Kabbalah that emerged in 13th-century Spain, traditionally attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. Complete Kabbalah text imported from Sefaria; the exact edition and licence are shown with each version.
historicalContext: Kabbalah is the Jewish mystical and theosophical tradition. Its works range from short speculative treatises to the multi-volume Zohar, and its language is symbolic rather than propositional.
availabilityNote: Imported from Sefaria. Version, source and licence are recorded per edition.
